ui_bugs.component: prefers-reduced-motion — .xu-dash class on SVG dash paths (HomePage.jsx hero flow, IntelligenceShowcase.jsx)
ui_bugs.issue: Under emulated `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `.flow-x`, the intelligence-flow strip and connectivity-bridge SVGs all correctly report animation-name:none, but `.xu-dash` still reports computed animation-name='xu-dash' with duration 1.2s. The @media rule in index.css:198 includes `.xu-dash` with `animation: none !important`, so the rule is present but not taking effect on the first .xu-dash element queried. Likely cause: React inline `style={{ animationDelay: '0.5s' }}` on some paths interacting with the shorthand reset, or the class being applied to an SVG element where the media rule specificity is being overridden. Recommend switching the reduced-motion rule to explicit longhands (`animation-name: none !important; animation-duration: 0s !important;`) OR adding the class to a wrapping group instead of individual paths.
scrollWidth=322 vs clientWidth=320 → 2px horizontal overflow at 320px. Not visible, but fails a strict 'no horizontal overflow ANYWHERE' check. 390px is clean (390/390).

rca_of_the_issue: 1) .xu-dash under reduced-motion: the CSS `.xu-dash { animation: none !important }` inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) is present in index.css:203 but computed style still shows animation-name='xu-dash'. Suspected cause is that .xu-dash is applied to SVG <path> elements which additionally carry inline style={{animationDelay: '0.5s'}} — the shorthand `animation: none` on the class should reset name+duration, but browsers can behave inconsistently when the shorthand is overridden by longhand inline styles + !important. Fix: use explicit `animation-name: none !important; animation-duration: 0s !important;` (longhands) inside the media query, OR wrap the animated paths in a <g class='xu-dash'> and stop applying inline animation-delay. 2) 320px 2px overflow is likely a max-width or padding miscalculation in one of the chapter grids at ultra-narrow viewports.
